acceptance.output_evidence:
THE READING, s.3 of the record, four questions and a fifth section.

3a. CAN A CONSUMER REJECT? Yes at the manifest, not yet at a served surface. Three refusals are now expressible. The weakest and most useful: `artifact_claim != "served_projection"` -- a consumer can refuse an interim or historical store outright without knowing how either was built. This is exactly the refusal E-3 wanted and could not have, because its two claim cards were written by a helper only two of four producers called, so a consumer reading a card-less manifest could not tell 'not a served projection' from 'nobody said'. Now it can: the absent case renders `!! provenance_claim: absent` and reads `edge_count_semantics=absent` IN A FIELD -- not as a missing key that .get() turns into None and a truthiness test turns into 'fine'. The sharper: `edge_count_semantics == "attempted"` means the number is an UPPER BOUND, so any consumer comparing two edge counts (a parity check, a drift alarm, a 'did tonight lose edges' question) has been silently comparing an upper bound against a true count whenever one side is a stitch store. Read site: one dict lookup on read_manifest(db), no engine. The strongest, and new in kind: bytes_written_at + content_sha256 let a consumer refuse a manifest THAT NO LONGER DESCRIBES THE BYTES BESIDE IT -- every other field describes the build; these two describe the BINDING, which is the thing that actually goes stale. HONEST LIMIT: all three are AVAILABLE to a consumer that reads; none is ENFORCED anywhere. S53's consuming half is now possible, not yet mandatory, and this cell was not scoped to make it so.

3b. WHAT THE SERVED HEADER SHOWS THE MORNING AFTER F-4: NOTHING -- and this is the answer I would most want the L9 seat to check. F-4's derive will call this writer and its manifest WILL carry stored / served_projection / a content_sha256 / a bytes_written_at, which rendered is arm 1 above. But NOTHING RENDERS IT: repo-wide there is one definition of format_provenance_header and three live call sites -- two in test files (.tools/tests/test_cg8_seam_retired_battery.py:268,277) and one in org/tier2_senior/0.8.0_AE_CloudComp/deliverables/l1a_item1b/sensor_kuzu_schema_residue.py:280. Neither projection_client.py nor projection_server.py nor kuzu_cli.py references _provenance AT ALL (0 hits across 3 files scanned); projection_server.py parses a DIFFERENT manifest schema (pointer / manifest_sha256 / age_line / vintage / committed_at, :109-187) that write_manifest does not produce. So C-S27's observation that the served header 'still reads 1166 nodes / 2488 edges with nothing beside it' describes a header no serving path emits at all. The morning after F-4 lands, an operator sees what they see today; a seat calling format_provenance_header by hand sees the full claim. The gap is a WIRING cell and it is not this one (NFRA_CLDGRPH-W3-S14). Caution for whoever cuts it: content_sha256 on a large served store is not free and the header renders on EVERY invocation -- this implementation already refuses above 64 MiB and PRINTS the skip, but a serve path should compare mtime only and reach for the hash on demand.

3c. WHAT THE LEGACY ALIAS COSTS AND WHEN IT RETIRES: one spelling of one concept alive in two forms for one round, READ-ONLY, rendered '(legacy key)' so it is never invisible. The cost is a READING cost: a future seat searching for edge_count_semantics misses the two E-3 cards on disk, and a schema census counts two keys where the taxonomy has one. The mitigation is that the writer can only produce the NEW spelling, so the legacy set is CLOSED at exactly the manifests already on disk -- it cannot grow. IT RETIRES WHEN no manifest on disk carries edge_count_claim: concretely, when the two main-workspace claim cards' stores (F-1's and F-6's) are retired or rebuilt through this writer. Naming the TRIGGER matters more than naming a date -- 'one round' is how a legacy key becomes permanent. ONE THING FOR THE RETIRING SEAT: E-3's cards spell the VALUE 'merge_attempts' while this vocabulary spells it 'attempted', and the reader passes the legacy value through VERBATIM rather than translating it, so a card renders 'edge_count_semantics=merge_attempts (legacy key)'. That is honest -- it shows what is actually written -- but it means the closed vocabulary is closed only for values THIS writer produced.

3d. COULD `!! BYTES NEWER THAN MANIFEST` FALSE-FIRE ON A LEGITIMATE COPY? YES, and this is the arm most likely to cry wolf. The mechanism: the projection worker fetches a store from S3 and writes it locally; the manifest was written by the PRODUCER stamping the PRODUCER's local mtime; the copy's local mtime is the COPY time, necessarily later, often by hours. S3 HAS NO CLIENT-SETTABLE MTIME FOR A DOWNLOADED OBJECT -- `aws s3 cp` sets the local mtime to now unless the caller restores it -- so the false fire is not a possibility, it is the DEFAULT on any copy path that does not think about it. Three bounds, none eliminating it: (i) the disciplinary answer is that a copy path should re-stamp the manifest through this writer after landing the bytes (correct: the local store's binding IS new) or preserve mtimes deliberately; (ii) THE HASH IS THE DISCRIMINATOR and it is already computed -- a false fire has content_sha256 MATCHING and only the mtime moved, a true fire usually has both moved -- but this implementation checks mtime FIRST and returns on the loud arm without consulting the hash, which is the cheap ordering and the WRONG one for exactly this case; a serve-path cell should invert it (mtime newer AND hash differs -> !! BYTES NEWER; mtime newer but hash matches -> a quieter 'bytes-vs-manifest: copied (mtime moved, content identical)'); (iii) the 2.0 s tolerance handles filesystem granularity and nothing else -- it is no defence against a copy. I did not make the inversion here because it changes what the arm MEANS rather than whether it works, and it costs a hash on every render, which is a serve-path decision rather than a writer one. Nobody is currently exposed: per 3b, no serve path renders this header yet.

3e. WHAT THIS ORDER DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO: did not touch kuzu_load.py (F-1's, outside the grant) though it is STILL PRESENT and its write_manifest call WILL raise TypeError on the required kwargs the moment it runs -- stated in the census output and the record rather than fixed, because it is the one way this cell's edit can break a file it is forbidden to touch; did not edit projection_server.py (it needs no edit, and finding out why is W3-S14); did not run any loader, open any store with an engine, or touch a main-workspace store or manifest; did not correct _provenance.py's module docstring where it claims kuzu_cli.py prints this header on every comp-kuzu invocation (measured: it does not) -- correcting the sentence without the wiring moves a false claim rather than removing it, and the wiring is out of grant; did not give test_kuzu_incremental_refresh.py a pytest-collectable surface, which would open kuzu engines the BOUNDS forbid outright (W3-S16, routed to the lane).
